headline: Navajo Nation Entry and Guided Tour Coordination
reservation: Access to the Valley Drive is managed by Navajo Nation Parks & Recreation and requires a separate entry fee from national park passes. While the main overlook is typically accessible during park hours, specialized guided tours into restricted areas like Mystery Valley or for sunrise/sunset photography should be booked well in advance through authorized Navajo operators. Check official tribal park bulletins as road conditions or cultural observances can alter access suddenly.

days.title: Mittens and Tribal Traditions

stops.name: The Mittens Overlook
stops.detail: Begin at the main visitor area to witness the scale of East and West Mitten Buttes from a stable, paved vantage point.

stops.name: Navajo Guided Backcountry Tour
stops.detail: Join an authorized Navajo guide to reach restricted arches and petroglyphs not accessible on the public driving loop.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours for the loop; conditions vary with sand and washouts.
days.note: Note that the Navajo Nation observes Daylight Saving Time, unlike the rest of Arizona.

days.title: Geology and Desert Paths
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from The View Hotel

stops.name: Wildcat Trail
stops.detail: Walk the only self-guided trail in the park, a 4-mile loop providing a floor-level perspective of the sandstone spires.

stops.name: Valley Drive Loop
stops.detail: Navigate the 17-mile unpaved road to see John Ford’s Point and the Totem Pole formations.

days.driving: Low-clearance vehicles should exercise caution; allow 3 hours for the scenic loop.
days.note: Check for blowing dust or heat restrictions before starting the Wildcat Trail.

days.title: High Desert Horizons

stops.name: Forrest Gump Point
stops.detail: View the iconic long-distance highway perspective of the valley from the Utah side of the border.

stops.name: Goulding's Trading Post Museum
stops.detail: Explore the history of film and commerce in the region through these historic buildings and exhibits.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the cross-border transit; conditions vary with wind.
days.note: Respect private homes and livestock when stopping along Highway 163.

intel.title: Visitor Center Hub
intel.text: The primary parking area is located at the tribal visitor center near the Mittens overlook. During peak fall and spring months, arrive before mid-morning to secure a space near the interpretive displays.

intel.title: Cellular Limitations
intel.text: Coverage is intermittent and often drops entirely once you descend onto the valley floor. Download offline maps and confirm your tour meeting point while in Kayenta or Mexican Hat.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: Refuel in Kayenta or Mexican Hat before entering the tribal park boundaries. There are no gas stations within the scenic loop area, and desert distances can be deceiving.

intel.title: Park Gate Hours
intel.text: Opening and closing times for the Valley Drive change seasonally and may not align with sunrise or sunset. Verify current gate closures locally to avoid being locked inside the loop road.

intel.title: Road Surface Variability
intel.text: The Valley Drive is unpaved with significant rocky stretches and loose sand. Conditions change rapidly after rain; high-clearance vehicles are recommended for independent driving.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental in Cortez or Phoenix and stock up on water and snacks in Kayenta before checking into your lodge near the park entrance.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance SUVs are best for the sandy Valley Drive; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved tribal roads.
plan.goldenHour: Merrick Butte from the visitor center terrace; timing varies significantly between winter and summer solstice.
